title: Build: Add eval harness for Storybook agentic setup
body:
Closes https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/34295 (M0 milestone)

## What I did

Eval harness to measure how well AI agents complete Storybook setup after `npx storybook@latest init --yes` on real-world projects. Primary metric: **ghost stories** (do rendered components actually work).

### Architecture

```
eval.ts          — single run:     node scripts/eval/eval.ts -p mealdrop
eval-parallel.ts — all 8 combos:   node scripts/eval/eval-parallel.ts -p mealdrop
```

**Pipeline per run:** copy from cache → run agent → grade (build + typecheck + ghost stories + setup patterns + changed files) → save to Google Sheets

### Agents (via SDK, not CLI)

| Agent | SDK | Models |
|-------|-----|--------|
| claude | `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` | sonnet-4.6, opus-4.6, haiku-4.5 |
| codex | `@openai/codex-sdk` | gpt-5.4 |

Agent is inferred from model: `-m gpt-5.4` auto-selects codex.

### Four independent axes

```
agent × model × effort × prompt
```

- **Effort**: low, medium, high, max (maps to Claude `effort` / Codex `model_reasoning_effort`)
- **Prompts**: `setup` (default), `self-heal` (vitest-based iteration loop)

### Parallel execution

`eval-parallel.ts` spawns 8 separate node processes (4 models × 2 prompts) with live-streamed prefixed logs:
```
[sonnet-4.6+setup] 🚀 Session started
[gpt-5.4+self-heal] 🔧 $ npx vitest run...
[opus-4.6+setup] 💬 I'll analyze the project...
```

### Pre-prepared repos

6 forked repos with `eval-baseline` branches (storybook already initialized):
- **mealdrop** — styled-components, Redux, React Router
- **edgy** — Tailwind, HeadlessUI, React Router
- **wikitok** — simple Tailwind
- **baklava** — component library, Zustand
- **echarts** — ECharts React wrapper
- **evergreen-ci** — GraphQL workspace

First run clones + installs → caches. Subsequent runs copy from cache — agent starts immediately.

### Grading

- **Ghost stories** — discovers candidate components, runs vitest with `STORYBOOK_COMPONENT_PATHS` to auto-generate and test stories (mirrors core-server implementation)
- **Storybook build** — pass/fail
- **TypeScript errors** — count
- **Setup patterns** — detects tailwind, redux, router, styled-components, etc.
- **Changed files** — git diff from baseline

### Results

- Structured `summary.json` per trial
- Google Sheets upload (set `EVAL_GOOGLE_SHEETS_URL`)
- Run ID / Upload ID for grouping
- Environment capture (node version, git info)

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: Kept this in Zod, but simplified `eval.ts` back down to the original flat flow. The agent-specific defaults now still come from `AGENTS`, and the rest of the CLI stays in the straightforward early-return structure.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: We probably wanna share the rationale of adding `.ts` with the team (maybe open a PR for `tsconfig` now?) so they can flag potential side effects (will Node 20 trip up?), and/or so they can also start applying `.ts`.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: nit: potential formatting setup issue. check if fmt job passes in CI?

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
nit: worth grouping up into the place where you define default effort, so we have a centralised definition for all the parameters that affect eval output.

At the `lib/agents` level I would find it normal that every parameter is mandatory, so that the dispatcher calling the agents has to centralise params by design.

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: Done. The per-agent defaults and execution settings now live in `AGENTS`, and `eval.ts` reads model/effort defaults from there instead of hardcoding them.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
1: Same here, we might wanna centralise this if possible (but I suppose those are agent specific)?

2: I saw agents run `mv` or `rm`, will these be included by default in the Bash tool?

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: Grouped these with the other agent execution knobs in `AGENTS`. For Claude the harness-level Bash toggle now lives next to the tool allowlist, and the comment there calls out that individual shell commands still flow through Claude's Bash tool.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: q: Is there any sense in wrapping this in a try-catch block so we can write partial run transcripts if there is a crash/error?

comments.author: yannbf
comments.body: Good catch

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: Done. Both drivers now write `transcript.json` from a `finally` block so we still keep partial transcripts when a run errors mid-stream.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: q: Is that consistent with the permissions for Claude?

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: Made this explicit in `AGENTS` as well. Claude now documents its tool-allowlist permission model and Codex its `approvalPolicy: "never"` model, so the difference is visible in one place.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: As we discussed, we should check what the most common default effort is.

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: Done. The default effort is `medium` now, and `eval.ts` reads defaults from `AGENTS` so the CLI and tests stay aligned.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: Missing pricing data for Claude

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: I left pricing empty for Claude on purpose because Claude already reports `total_cost_usd` from the SDK. The pricing table here is only for manual estimation when the driver doesn't return cost natively.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: nit: For completeness, should those thresholds also be stored alongside the raw data/scores in results? Or I guess if we have the raw data we can already recompute new scores and it's fine.

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: Good idea, but I left this out of the current pass. Right now we can recompute from the raw data; persisting thresholds and weights would be a nice follow-up for reproducibility.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
is that a `tail` function?

Do we have any counterpoints to tailing build logs, @yannbf? Might we be missing data?

comments.author: yannbf
comments.body: I think it's fine because this is only used in this file for build and type checking, at 2000 characters cut.

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: Yep, effectively a tail helper. I kept it because the full build/typecheck logs are still written to files; this truncation is only for the summary payload we surface inline.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:

@kasperpeulen if you still have LLM credits to spare, could your agent inject git HEAD ref IDs into its cache keys? 😆

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: Addressed. The repo cache now stores repo/branch/baseline metadata and refreshes when the remote `eval-baseline` head moves, so branch updates won't silently reuse stale clones.

comments.body: nit: I'd prefer using https://www.npmjs.com/package/cachedir or similar so the files end up in `~/.cache/storybook-eval` rather than a sibling folder to the repo. Feel free to ignore this tho

comments.body: I think it's fine to not add yet another dependency to the repo, and by having it easily accessible we can debug the projects if something goes wrong

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body: Leaving the current cache path for now. I agree with keeping it easy to inspect/debug without adding another dependency here.
